guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul Standard / Fender Telecaster / Danelectro
guitar.evidence: Jimmy Page's 1959 Gibson Les Paul ('Number One') is one of the most iconic guitars in rock history, alongside his well-documented use of a Telecaster (Stairway to Heaven solo) and Danelectro for alternate tunings.

tone.target: raw Page-style riff tone with biting upper mids and light fuzz edge
tone.profile: raw Page-style riff tone with biting upper mids and light fuzz edge
tone.summary: A classic Marshall/Plexi-style chain using a slight OD boost for grit, followed by the UK 45 amp model, paired with a tight 4x12 cabinet to capture the aggressive, mid-focused riff tone of 'Immigrant Song'.
corrections: favor dry British crunch over high-gain

rig.name: Led Zeppelin - Immigrant Song - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and unwanted noise from aggressive riffing.
Provide the necessary grit and bite (slight fuzz edge) without sounding like a Big Muff.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used to simulate the slight overdriven character of vintage Marshall amps, providing mid-range punch.

alternatives.reason: A slightly cleaner option if more bite is needed.

blocks.purpose: Reserved for heavier sections or alternative tones; kept off to maintain the raw crunch.
blocks.gap: The primary grit is handled by Green OD. This slot remains available if more aggressive distortion is required later in the song structure.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Marshall/Plexi tone required for raw British crunch and mid-focus.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative, but UK 45 is more classically associated with the desired tone.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British cabinet sound and tight low end.
Sculpt the tone by boosting upper mids for 'riff-forward bite' and controlling low end tightness.
Not required for this riff tone; kept off.
Avoid lush effects; kept off to maintain raw punch.
Avoid lush delay as per instructions; kept off.
Avoid big reverb; kept off to maintain dry punch.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR to better capture the raw, aggressive bite and mid-focus required for Zeppelin's riffing.

proposals.reason: Enhance the raw, biting upper mids and aggressive character of the tone.
